_README: The kit's blessed versions, and the conditions under which each one applies.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the kit is a platform. It ships configs, CI jobs and a
library standard, and a platform that asserts a tool has to pin it — otherwise
every project answers 'which version do we run?' on its own and the fleet
silently diverges. The rule is one line:
THE KIT PINS WHAT THE KIT SHIPS, OR WHAT THE KIT'S CHOICES DRAG IN.
That second clause is not decoration. `zod` is nobody's declared dependency in
some repos and is still the sharpest version trap in this stack, because
better-auth and TanStack Start's build need v4 while shadcn's CLI pulls v3 — and the loser of
that hoist fails at RUNTIME, not at build.
Anything the kit says nothing about stays the project's own call, handled by
Dependabot and the dependency-triage pass. This file is not a list of every
dependency; it is the list the kit refuses to let drift.
EXACT VERSIONS, NOT RANGES. A caret lets a fresh install drift to a version the
kit never blessed, defeating lockstep silently — and `npm install` ADDS a caret
by default, which is how it keeps coming back. `whenResolved` entries are the
exception and pin a MAJOR, because a transitively-dragged package's exact
version is not the project's to choose.
EACH ENTRY CARRIES ITS OWN TRIGGER, and the trigger is what makes 'opinionated
but does not block unless it matters' mechanical rather than a convention:
applies: 'whenDeclared'        this project declares it -> it must be ours
applies: {whenFile: [...]}     a kit-shipped config is present -> the tool
behind it must be pinned. No config, no opinion.
applies: 'whenResolved'        it is anywhere in the lockfile, transitive
included -> one major across the whole tree.
severity: 'required'           a violation fails the build
severity: 'advisory'           a violation prints and passes — for a real
problem the fleet has not adopted the fix for yet
installedBy: 'project'         a declared dependency; the guard checks package.json
installedBy: 'ci'              installed by a workflow at run time; this file owns
the version and CI reads it, so no project declares it
ENFORCEMENT is scripts/check-stack.mjs (CI job `stack-standard`) — hermetic,
reads manifests and the lockfile, never the network.
`blessed_at` is the date of the last full TanStack review. Entries added since
carry their own `blessedAt`, so one date never claims a review that did not happen.
MOVING A PIN is /review-stack: read what changed between our version and latest,
decide whether it affects how WE use it, and update whatever references it
invalidates. Never bump this file to make a build pass.
_node_notes: The one Node major every project runs: its .nvmrc names it, its root engines.node
allows nothing older, and every Dockerfile node: image and CI node-version names it.
The kit moves it to the next Active LTS major — Active LTS when lts <= today <= maintenance in
migration that moves every project at once.

vite.why: TanStack Start peers vite >=8.0.0 with no upper bound, so without a pin a fresh install would take a Vite major the kit has never run. Two copies of Vite in one tree make the router's instance checks fail and every route 404 (dependency-management.md); the lockfile check compares each declaring workspace's resolved copy against this one.

better-auth.why: Better Auth holds the front door, and its breaking changes are invisible until a version boundary. It validates the auth schema it is given against its own model and rejects authentication requests on a mismatch — a missing column, or a required column it never writes — so a schema that was right for one version can lock every user out on the next. A caret range walks a project across that boundary on a fresh install with no commit to blame. Pin exactly, and treat every bump as a change that re-checks the auth tables: `npx auth check schema` reports every mismatch without changing anything.

@biomejs/biome.why: The kit ships biome.json AND a CI biome check, so the kit owns the linter. biome.json's $schema names a version; a different binary reads that config as something else. Worse, a project that declares nothing at all gets `npx biome` resolving to an UNRELATED package of that name on npm which exits 0 — a lint gate that passes without linting, locally and on a runner.

@commitlint/cli.why: pr-title.yml installs this at run time. Unpinned, that executes whatever the registry serves under the name, and --no-save leaves no record of what ran. This file owns the version and the guard asserts the workflow names it, so the two cannot drift apart.

@commitlint/config-conventional.why: pr-title.yml installs this at run time. Unpinned, that executes whatever the registry serves under the name, and --no-save leaves no record of what ran. This file owns the version and the guard asserts the workflow names it, so the two cannot drift apart.

@google/design.md.why: The kit's design-system discipline makes design.md the spec, and CI runs `npm run lint:design` (`design.md lint design.md`) whenever it exists. The linter's rules change between pre-1.0 minors, so an unpinned one passes a spec on one machine and fails it on another.

esbuild.why: The kit's claude-design engine bundles the design system with it, resolved from the UI package. A different version emits a different bundle for the same source, so the published system would change with no code change behind it.

knip.why: The kit ships knip.config.ts and the CI knip check, so the kit owns the tool. The config is written against knip 6's schema and plugin behaviour: which entries a plugin contributes, how includeEntryExports treats a workspace's exports map, how ignoreIssues matches. Another version reads the same file differently and the gate reports a different set of findings with no change in the code. The job installs it at run time; this file owns the version and the guard asserts the workflow names it.

pyright.why: The CI python job typechecks from the repository root whenever a root pyrightconfig.json or pyproject.toml exists, so the kit owns the checker. Pyright adds and tightens checks in patch releases, so two versions report different errors on the same code. The job installs this version over whatever the project declares; the commit gate warns when the pyright installed locally differs. The guard asserts the workflow names it.

vitest.why: The kit owns the test configuration (templates/testing/vitest.config.ts and the files beside it), written against vitest 5's projects API: inline projects extend the root config and share its Vite server unless they change the Vite config, and `vitest related` reports "No affected test files found" when nothing reaches a change. A project on another major reads the same config differently, so the version is the kit's. Vitest 5 takes vite as a required peer, so a project declares the kit's vite beside it.

@neondatabase/api-client.why: The kit's templates/testing/globalSetup.ts creates and deletes the integration branch through it. Before 2.7.2 deleteProjectBranch took positional arguments, so the kit's object-argument call requests /projects/undefined/branches/undefined, 404s, and leaks a branch every run.

pg.why: The Postgres driver under drizzle-orm/node-postgres, and the kit's templates/testing/integration-helpers.ts imports it directly. Its next major adopts libpq semantics, where sslmode=require stops verifying the certificate: nothing fails, TLS still negotiates, and verification is silently gone. Every connection seam pins verify-full against that, and the version that seam was proven on is this one. Pin exactly so the fleet runs the driver it tested, and treat the major as a change that re-checks every connection seam.

_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-table: v9, GA 2026-08-04. v8 is NOT the conservative alternative — its last release was 8.21.3 on 2025-04-14. Do not use legacyCreateColumnHelper: it is the v8 compatibility shim, and new code has no use for it.
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query: Glue package. Sole export setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({router, queryClient}) — wires QueryClientProvider plus SSR dehydrate/hydrate/streaming. Required wherever Query is used with Start.
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-form-start: Start integration for Form: formOptions, createServerValidate, getFormData, mergeForm. Versioned in lockstep with react-form.
_packages_notes.vite: Pinned for the app's own build; the kit ships no app vite.config. @vitejs/plugin-react is the project's choice: 5.2 and 6.x both accept Vite 8.

banned.react-hook-form: Use @tanstack/react-form. NOTE: `npx shadcn add form` installs this as a hard dependency — do not use shadcn's form atom; build field components against TanStack Form instead.

_form_rule: Form-library adoption is decided PER APP, all-in within an app. Three states,
and the third is a hard failure:
1. app declares @tanstack/react-form           -> decided, nothing to record
2. app listed in FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS          -> deliberately decided no
3. app in neither                              -> question never asked, FAIL
FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS is a space-separated app-name list in
.claude/sync-substitutions.json, read at runtime (same shape as DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS).
Exempt suits apps with no real data entry — ecommerce/cart surfaces, marketing
pages, and control-plane/service apps whose UI is a couple of status screens.
Data-entry apps (ERP browses and record forms) take the library.

_references_notes: DISTILLED, not copied. Our subset in our words, scoped to what business
applications need. `distilled_from` records which upstream skills were read, so
/review-stack knows what to re-read when a pin moves; an empty list means
there is no upstream for it.
NOT CARRIED, deliberately: every migrate-* skill (one-offs — SKILL.md says where
to read one), server-components (we do not use RSC), offline persistence,
SCOPE RULE: if we do not use a feature, it does not get pages explaining how the
feature works. Upstream already documents it and node_modules already has it.

@tanstack/query-intent.why: TanStack/query PR #10879 (29 Query skills in a new @tanstack/query-intent package) was closed unmerged on 2026-08-17 with no replacement, and react-query ships no skills. The only upstream Query guidance for agents is react-router's compositions/router-query skill, which exists in the router repo but is not in the published package (its files are dist and src). queries-and-mutations.md stays ours.
@tanstack/query-intent.action: When router-query is published, or Query ships skills of its own, re-distil queries-and-mutations.md against it and keep only our decisions on top.

start-middleware.why: We deliberately do NOT use createMiddleware for auth (server-functions.md). #2783 — server middleware in the client bundle — was open Nov 2024 to Feb 2026. Still open as of 2026-10-16: #7213 (middleware calling a server function in another file throws; a 2026-09 comment reports it hanging in production on Vite 8 — unverified) and #7459 (createMiddleware undefined on cold-start SSR in vite dev, labelled needs-upstream-fix).
start-middleware.action: If both close, the technical objection is gone — but the decision still needs a reason to adopt beyond saving lines. Middleware's only real capability over a handler-top call is running code AFTER the handler. Re-open only when something genuinely needs wrapping.

@tanstack/react-form reset.why: Open defects in what forms.md prescribes after a save (formApi.reset(value)): #2228 resetting an array field to a shorter array does not re-render; #2381 async validation reapplies stale errors after reset(); #2384 a pre-reset validation clears a newer run's isValidating. Each has an open fix PR.
@tanstack/react-form reset.action: When the fixes ship in a 1.x release, bump react-form and react-form-start together.
